title: He Had Strength… But Lost His Soul to Attraction
paragraphs:
He Had Strength… But Lost His Soul to Attraction
The Untold Truth About Samson That Still Exposes Us Today
There are moments in Scripture that feel less like history… and more like a mirror you weren’t ready to look into.
Samson is one of them.

Not because of his strength…
But because of his weakness.
Because if we’re honest—deeply, painfully honest—most people don’t fall away from God in a moment of rebellion.
They drift… through attraction.
It started quietly for Samson.

The Hebrew text doesn’t soften it. In Judges 14:1, it says:
“וַיֵּרֶד שִׁמְשׁוֹן תִּמְנָתָה… וַיַּרְא אִשָּׁה”
Vayered Shimshon Timnatah… vayar ishah
“Samson went down to Timnah… and he saw a woman.”
He saw.
That’s where it began.

Not with sin.
Not with betrayal.
Not with destruction.
Just… seeing.
Attraction is not evil.

But what you do with what you see…
That’s where everything changes.
Samson didn’t just notice her. He demanded her.
“Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes.” (Judges 14:3)
Right in my eyes.

Not God’s will.
Not God’s standard.
Not God’s calling.
Just… what felt right.
And if that doesn’t hit something deep inside you… it should.
Because we’ve all had moments where something felt right… but wasn’t righteous.
Moments where we said, “I know what God says… but this feels different.”
Moments where attraction started to rewrite conviction.
You don’t fall overnight.
You fall when your eyes begin to lead your soul.
The Greek word used in the New Testament for this kind of desire is “ἐπιθυμία” (epithymia)—a longing, a craving, a pull that can either be surrendered to God… or allowed to consume you.

James 1:14-15 says it plainly:
“ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται… ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος”
“But each person is tempted when they are dragged away by their own desire and enticed.”
Dragged.
That’s what attraction can become when it’s not surrendered.

Not a gentle suggestion…
But a force.

Samson didn’t guard his eyes…
So his eyes guided his life.
And slowly, almost invisibly, the man chosen by God began to trade purpose for pleasure.

The same man who tore apart a lion…
Couldn’t tear himself away from what he wanted.
Let that sit with you.

Strength in public…
Weakness in private.
He played with compromise like it wasn’t dangerous.

He touched what he wasn’t supposed to touch.
He entertained what he wasn’t supposed to entertain.
He lingered where he wasn’t supposed to stay.

And eventually…
He loved what God never told him to love.
Delilah wasn’t the beginning of his fall.
She was the exposure of a pattern.
A pattern of choosing what felt good… over what was God.

Judges 16:1 says:
“וַיֵּלֶךְ שִׁמְשׁוֹן עַזָּתָה וַיַּרְא־שָׁם אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה”
“Samson went to Gaza… and saw there a prostitute.”
Again…
He saw.
And he went.
Attraction had become direction.
And direction… became destruction.
The most terrifying verse in Samson’s life isn’t when his hair was cut.
It’s when he didn’t even realise God had left him.

“וְהוּא לֹא יָדַע כִּי יְהוָה סָר מֵעָלָיו”
“He did not know that the Lord had departed from him.” (Judges 16:20)
Read that again.
He didn’t know.
That’s what unchecked attraction does.
It numbs you.

It convinces you you’re still strong…
While you’re already empty.

It lets you keep moving…
Without realising you’ve lost what matters most.
Be honest.

Has something been pulling your attention lately…
More than God?

A person?
A relationship?
A secret habit?
A desire you’ve been justifying?
You didn’t plan to drift.
You just kept looking.
And now… it’s harder to look away.

Not for performance.
Not for religion.
But because honesty is where healing begins.
Samson lost his eyes… physically.

But long before that…
He had already lost vision spiritually.
That’s the real danger.
When attraction blinds you before it binds you.
But this isn’t where the story ends.
Because God doesn’t just write stories about failure.
He rewrites them into redemption.
In the lowest moment of Samson’s life—blind, broken, humiliated—he finally prays.

Not a long prayer.
Not a perfect prayer.
Just a real one.

“אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה זָכְרֵנִי נָא”
“Lord God, remember me, I pray…” (Judges 16:28)
Remember me.
That’s all he had left.

And somehow…
That was enough.
Because grace doesn’t wait for perfection.
It responds to surrender.
God didn’t restore Samson’s past.
He restored his purpose.

And in his final moment…
God used him again.

Stronger in surrender…
Than he ever was in self-confidence.
That’s the Gospel.
Not that you won’t be tempted.
But that Jesus steps into your weakness… and rewrites your ending.
Because where Samson failed…
Jesus didn’t.

Where Samson was led by what he saw…
Jesus was led by the Father.
Even when it cost Him everything.

The Aramaic cry from the cross echoes deeper than we realise:
“ܐܝܠ ܐܝܠ ܠܡܢܐ ܫܒܩܬܢܝ”
“Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?”
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

Jesus took the separation…
So you don’t have to live in it.

He took the consequence…
So your story doesn’t end in ruin.
That means no matter how far attraction has pulled you…
Grace can still bring you back.
Let this settle in your spirit:

Attraction isn’t the problem.
But unsurrendered attraction will quietly replace God… if you let it.

Guard your eyes.
Guard your heart.
Because what you keep looking at… will eventually shape what you live for.
If this hit something real inside you… don’t keep it to yourself.
That discomfort might be the very thing God uses to wake them up.
You’re going to need to come back to it on days when your flesh gets louder than your faith.
And if you want to go deeper—not just emotionally, but spiritually—walk closely with us.
And if you’re serious about growing in Christ, about fighting the battles you don’t talk about, about becoming who God actually called you to be…
Because supporting this mission isn’t about us.
It’s about making sure truth keeps reaching people who are one decision away from losing everything.
Don’t wait until you “feel ready.”
Samson waited too long.
And attraction nearly cost him everything.
One look can start a drift… but one surrender can start a resurrection.
